title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish.

reviewer.method: Entire primary main text consumed in two untruncated contiguous chunks; all four main figures, graphical abstract, all eight Table1 patient columns, and all nine supplementary PDF pages inspected in pixels. Complete supplement text, five tables and three figure plates read. Every mapped positive and negative assertion checked against individual columns; no outcomes consulted.

audit.exposure_note: Required HANDOFF contains aggregate compact-cohort metrics. No per-case inference ranks, scores or outcomes opened or used. Post-inference source audit, not blinded validation.

limitations: All distributed main/supplement components consumed; raw supporting data available only on request were not obtained, no contact made. Full reading does not remove scientific uncertainty or reproduce the experiments.

TableS4 classifies all three missense variants VUS. REVEL0.558/0.370/0.262, MutPred uncertain V427F and benign-supporting A509T; M-CAP/PrimateAI tolerate V427F. Multiple correlated in-silico predictions and AlphaFold/PremPS modelling do not independently prove damaging structure or function.

Four new patients from three families, two siblings not independent. Four prior patients are comparison summaries, not newly phenotyped; original historical papers not read in this review. No burden/control association test or full alternative-candidate list supplied. Large ROH37.4/13Mb can contain other candidates; no exclusion of all multilocus explanations.

Internal consanguinity conflict: narrative says2/3families, Table1 and pedigrees explicitly show only family1 consanguineous; family2 has13MbROH but reported no consanguinity. ROH alone does not establish known pedigree relationship.

Family3 parent-label inconsistency: Fig1A motherC/T and fatherG/A versus Results and Fig1D fatherR717Ter/motherA509T. Trans inheritance remains supported but precise parent assignment is qualified. Table1P4 slightly short CC does not support packet thinCC. Negative drooling/unsteady-gait claims generally reflect unreported features.

F0 crispants are mosaic with representative ICE91%indels/KO84, per-fish KO scores around60-85%; this is not a stable exact-allele homozygous line or proof every cell is biallelic null. Topfive predicted off-target loci negative bySanger do not exclude all off-target/editing effects. Authors explicitly call forF1line. ReducedRNA suggests but does not directly demonstrate NMD.

Morphology and behavioural analysis unblinded; random acquisition by coauthors does not erase observer bias. Sample size experience-based. Fish-level observations nested in experiments; overallMethods3replicates but figures pool fish counts without detailed hierarchical model.

Brain area reduced while gross head area nonsignificant in Fig3D. Fig3caption reverses panelsC/D relative to plotted eye/head labels. Smaller body/eye and brain do not establish a specific human microcephaly mechanism independent of generalized developmental effects.

HumanWTmRNA rescue supports conserved function; C172G/V427F fail efficient rescue. No protein-expression/abundance matching, no exact human patient model, and A509T/R717Ter untested. Fig4panels lack contemporaneous uninjectedKO control; rescue inference partly compares separate Fig3experiment. Nonsignificant WT-rescue difference is not equivalence; residual activity not quantified. No therapeutic rescue claim follows.

PTZ-induced relative locomotion is normalized to low basal swimming; altered baseline can amplify ratios. Elevated pERK is compatible with neuronal activation but not electrophysiological proof of seizures; no EEG recordings, and no pERKdifference at30minutes. Repeated minute-wise comparisons and field/cell sample structure limit inference.

POLR3 target/pre-tRNA abundance reductions measured in whole larvae pools20, N4-5, not direct nascent transcription rate or brain-specific target-gene program. Changes can reflect RNA turnover/development/cell composition. Methodsnormalizeelf1alpha but Fig4normalizeshprt; both primers supplied, exact normalization workflow not fully reconciled. ControlWT values fixed1 and nonparametric testing deserve paired-data clarification.

Graphical abstract eightpatients/sixfamilies combines new and historical subjects. Dysmorphic percentages in Results imply denominator9 (e.g.56%,89%,78%) despite eight total, unexplained. SupplementTable5 known-positive6/8microcephaly treats twoNA as denominator; absence of data is not absence. TableS5cerebellar4/6 aggregates hypoplasia/atrophy despite apparent six imaging descriptions with cerebellar involvement, unresolved count.
No comparative drug effectiveness or N1002K/BubR1 rescue tested. S1structure is prediction only; reported significant changes mean computational prediction, not measured conformational change.
